title: 155. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Interpreting Rates with Different Denominators
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Unit Rate in Pages per Minute
questions.learningObjective: Calculate and interpret a unit rate from a given total quantity and time.
questions.question: A printer prints \(180\) pages in \(6\) minutes. What is its printing rate in pages per minute?
questions.explanation:
The rate compares pages to minutes. Divide the number of pages by the number of minutes:
\(180\div 6=30\).
So the printer prints \(30\) pages per minute.
questions.hint: Divide the total number of pages by the total number of minutes.

questions.concept: Comparing Speeds with Different Time Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two rates by converting them to a common unit.
questions.question: Runner A completes \(400\text{ m}\) in \(40\) seconds. Runner B completes \(1\text{ km}\) in \(2\) minutes. Which runner is faster?
questions.explanation:
Convert both rates to meters per second.
Runner A: \(400\div 40=10\text{ m/s}\).
Runner B: \(1\text{ km}=1000\text{ m}\) and \(2\text{ minutes}=120\text{ seconds}\), so \(1000\div 120\approx 8.33\text{ m/s}\).
Since \(10>8.33\), Runner A is faster.
questions.hint: Convert both distances to meters and both times to seconds, then compare the speeds.

questions.concept: Rate with a Fractional Time Denominator
questions.learningObjective: Compute a unit rate when the time is given as a fraction.
questions.question: A copy machine copies \(3\) pages in \(\frac{1}{4}\) minute. What is its rate in pages per minute?
questions.explanation:
The rate is pages divided by minutes:
\(3\div\frac{1}{4}=3\times 4=12\).
So the machine copies \(12\) pages per minute.
questions.hint: A unit rate is the number of pages divided by the number of minutes. How many quarter-minutes are in one minute?

questions.concept: Comparing Prices with Different Quantity Denominators
questions.learningObjective: Compare unit prices when the quantities purchased are different.
questions.question: Store A sells \(5\text{ kg}\) of rice for \(40\text{ yuan}\). Store B sells \(3\text{ kg}\) of rice for \(27\text{ yuan}\). Which store has the lower price per kilogram?
questions.explanation:
Find the price per kilogram for each store.
Store A: \(40\div 5=8\text{ yuan/kg}\).
Store B: \(27\div 3=9\text{ yuan/kg}\).
Since \(8<9\), Store A has the lower price per kilogram.
questions.hint: Compute price divided by mass for each store, then compare the unit prices.

questions.concept: Scaling a Rate Given as Cups per Dozen
questions.learningObjective: Use a rate with a non-unit denominator to find a required quantity.
questions.question: A recipe uses \(2\) cups of flour for every \(3\) dozen cookies. How many cups of flour are needed for \(5\) dozen cookies at the same rate?
questions.explanation:
The rate is \(2\) cups per \(3\) dozen, or \(\frac{2}{3}\) cup per dozen.
For \(5\) dozen cookies:
\(5\times\frac{2}{3}=\frac{10}{3}=3\frac{1}{3}\) cups.
So \(3\frac{1}{3}\) cups of flour are needed.
questions.hint: First find the number of cups of flour needed for \(1\) dozen cookies.

questions.concept: Comparing Speeds with Different Time Denominators
questions.learningObjective: Compare average speeds by converting rates to the same time unit.
questions.question: A train travels \(90\text{ km}\) in \(1.5\) hours. A bus travels \(60\text{ km}\) in \(45\) minutes. Which vehicle has the greater average speed?
questions.explanation:
Convert both speeds to kilometers per hour.
Train: \(90\div 1.5=60\text{ km/h}\).
Bus: \(45\text{ minutes}=0.75\text{ hour}\), so \(60\div 0.75=80\text{ km/h}\).
Since \(80>60\), the bus has the greater average speed.
questions.hint: Convert \(45\) minutes to hours, then compare both speeds in km/h.

questions.concept: Applying a Rate with a Fractional Time Denominator
questions.learningObjective: Determine an output over a given time using a computed unit rate.
questions.question: A machine produces \(45\) parts in \(\frac{3}{4}\) hour. At the same rate, how many parts will it produce in \(2\) hours?
questions.explanation:
First find the rate in parts per hour:
\(45\div\frac{3}{4}=45\times\frac{4}{3}=60\) parts per hour.
In \(2\) hours, the machine produces:
\(60\times 2=120\) parts.
So it will produce \(120\) parts.
questions.hint: Find how many parts are produced in \(1\) hour, then multiply by \(2\).

questions.concept: Comparing Earnings Rates with Different Time Denominators
questions.learningObjective: Compare hourly earnings by calculating pay per hour.
questions.question: Worker A earns \(360\text{ yuan}\) in \(6\) hours. Worker B earns \(250\text{ yuan}\) in \(4\) hours. Which worker earns more per hour?
questions.explanation:
Find each worker's hourly earnings.
Worker A: \(360\div 6=60\text{ yuan}\) per hour.
Worker B: \(250\div 4=62.5\text{ yuan}\) per hour.
Since \(62.5>60\), Worker B earns more per hour.
questions.hint: Divide total earnings by total hours for each worker, then compare.

questions.concept: Using a Fuel Consumption Rate to Find Required Fuel
questions.learningObjective: Apply a given rate to calculate fuel needed for a different distance.
questions.question: A car uses \(8\) liters of fuel to travel \(100\text{ km}\). At the same rate, how many liters of fuel are needed to travel \(250\text{ km}\)?
questions.explanation:
The fuel consumption rate is \(8\) liters per \(100\text{ km}\), or \(0.08\) liter per km.
For \(250\text{ km}\):
\(0.08\times 250=20\) liters.
So \(20\) liters of fuel are needed.
questions.hint: Find the fuel used per kilometer, or set up the proportion \(\frac{8}{100}=\frac{x}{250}\).

questions.concept: Finding Total Time from a Fractional Work Rate
questions.learningObjective: Determine the time to complete one whole job from a fractional rate.
questions.question: A machine completes \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a job in \(\frac{3}{4}\) hour. At this rate, how many hours does it take to complete the whole job?
questions.explanation:
First find the work rate in jobs per hour:
\(\frac{2}{3}\div\frac{3}{4}=\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{4}{3}=\frac{8}{9}\) job per hour.
To complete \(1\) whole job, take the reciprocal of the rate:
\(1\div\frac{8}{9}=\frac{9}{8}\) hours.
So it takes \(\frac{9}{8}\) hours to complete the whole job.
questions.hint: Find the fraction of the job completed in \(1\) hour, then invert that rate to get the time for \(1\) whole job.
